title: More on dominated and microscopic sets
summary: Let $S$ be a family of sequences decreasing to zero. A set $E$ in a metric space is $S$-dominated if, for every $s\in S$, there exists a countable cover $\{E_n\}$ of $E$ such that $diam E_n<s_n$ for every $n$. We continue the study of families of dominated sets initiated in the previous paper. We look, e.g., into Cartesian products of dominated sets with strong measure and interaction of microscopic and porous sets.
